title: Untitled 3.0
description: This world shrinks into a speck.
story:
Whose barn this is I think I know.
They live out on the tranquil snow.
She fishes searching for her meal,
But swimming fast upstream they go.

A person tends a fire of steel,
Unconcerned about the ordeal.
A gentle growing tree still thrives,
Beneath the sun it starts to heal.

An owl flying high arrives,
Just as everyone survives
The overwhelming, winding trek
Of fragile life to stay alive.

A world away beyond this deck
We slave to all powerful tech.
With far too long a road to check
This world now shrinks into a speck.

title: Stranger Things (not the show)
story:
She had wandered off trail in the Bonair Forest, craving quiet from the other hikers’ chatter. Deeper and deeper she went, pushing through bushes and ferns, letting the forest close behind her.

She was lost in thought when a faint melody broke the calm.

A saxophone, somewhere ahead.

She moved toward it carefully, afraid to disrupt what she had stumbled upon. The music grew louder.

She stopped. Frozen and unseen.

A weathered sign, swallowed by moss, read Blahdell.

“Some hidden sanctuary”, she murmured.

The saxophonist sat on a sapphire blue rock, its surface smooth and luminous, as if it had fallen from somewhere else entirely. Her brows furrowed. Impossible.

An absurdly large butterfly perched on a tree. A single red tulip stood tall in her path, glowing faintly. Its scent sharp and strangely like Mrs. Meyer’s lavender hand soap. Nearby, a streetlamp burned steadily, casting no shadow at all. Indifferent to day or night. Off to the side, a tent sat empty.

Strange, she thought

She stayed perfectly still, afraid any movement might unravel the scene.

Through the trees, the Space Needle loomed, its base tangled in ferns… but it was off…

Then she noticed a hand high in the canopy, casually tossing lettuce onto the path.

“What the hell?” she breathed, stepping closer.

The butterfly stirred. It descended toward the lettuce and began to eat.

She tilted her head toward the sun, squinting through the thick canopy, trying to make out the owner of the arm.

The music stopped. Her stomach dropped.

Shit.

The saxophonist turned to her, voice low and urgent.

“Quick! Go back! Before they see you”.

The Space Needle began to flare blue.

A signal.

The hand withdrew. The streetlamp brightened. The tulip went dark. And the butterfly kept eating, unbothered.

A jet screamed overhead, too low, too fast.

She spun.

title: Denali, Alaska
description: In my underworld there is a red dragon.
story:
The purple and blue hues of the sunset call to me. Below, the river mirrors the sky so perfectly.

Still, something unsettles me.

Through the fog, a narrow stream leads me to a black opening carved into the land. Someone stands in the doorway, and I can’t tell if they have found their way out or are stepping into a journey that has just begun.

Hands break the surface, grasping, reaching. It seems others have tried this crossing before.

A solitary figure drifts by in a small raft, and I wonder if they take passengers. Despite the surrounding peril, their stillness feels grounding. Others watch from above, some curious, some ready to act.

I want to know what lies beyond the mountain. I hope it is good, but I doubt it.

Experimenting with this kind of writing is fun, bringing my work to life in a new way. I want to hint at a story without explaining it outright. One of the reasons I love collaging is that I can piece together unrelated elements and let them form meaning in unexpected ways. :-)
